# `silk/http/websocket_stream`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

WebSocket sessions over a byte duplex, for clients and servers, with a split form for fibers.

## When to use
After an opening handshake, make a [`WebSocket`](#WebSocket) around the connection with [`WebSocket.make`](#WebSocket.impl.make).
Then call [`WebSocket.readEvent`](#WebSocket.impl.readEvent) in a loop, and answer with [`WebSocket.writeText`](#WebSocket.impl.writeText) or
[`WebSocket.writeBinary`](#WebSocket.impl.writeBinary). `silk.http.websocket_client` and `silk.http.websocket_upgrade` do the
handshake and make the session for you.

When one fiber must wait for messages while other fibers send, split the session with
[`fromHalves`](#fromHalves). The [`ReadHalf`](#ReadHalf) reads and answers Pings and Closes, and each [`WriteHalf`](#WriteHalf) (clone it
for each fiber) sends. Writes from several fibers are sent one at a time, never mixed.

## Details
A session reads into its own buffer, and keeps the bytes that came after a frame for the next
call. Each `readEvent` returns one complete event:
- `Text` and `Binary`: the message is in [`WebSocket.message`](#WebSocket.impl.message) until the next `readEvent`.
- `Ping`: the Pong was already sent.
- `Pong`: the payload of a Pong.
- `Close`: the peer sent Close. The answer Close was already sent, and the session is `Closed`.
  Close the connection.

A frame that breaks a rule fails the call with `Protocol`. Before that, the session sends a
Close with the code of the error. Every later call fails.

## Errors
[`StreamError`](#StreamError) keeps the frame error or the transport error. `OutOfMemoryError` if a buffer
cannot grow.

## Gotchas
- A deadline applies to one call. A read that passes its deadline fails the session, as any
  transport error does.
- The session does not close the transport. Close it when the session is `Closed` or failed.

## Examples
### Answer a message over a memory duplex
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.io.memory_byte_duplex { MemoryByteDuplex, MemoryReadEvent, MemoryWriteAction, MemoryWriteEvent }
import silk.system.monotonic_clock { MonotonicClock }
import silk.system.monotonic_clock_native { OsMonotonicClock }
import silk.system.random { Random }
import silk.system.random_native { OsRandom }
import silk.system.system_clock { Instant, SystemClock }
import silk.http.transport as Transport
import silk.http.websocket { Event, Opcode, Role, appendFrame }
import silk.http.websocket_stream { Options, StreamError, WebSocket }

effect fn program() -> i32
  ! StreamError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator | &mut MonotonicClock | &mut Random {
  // The client sends one masked Text frame, and the server accepts all writes.
  let mut wire = Bytes.make()
  run appendFrame(&mut wire, Opcode.Text, true, b"ping", Option<[u8; 4]>.some([9, 8, 7, 6]))
  let mut reads = List<MemoryReadEvent>.make()
  run reads.append(MemoryReadEvent.Data {readyAt: SystemClock.make(0, 0), bytes: move wire})
  let mut writes = List<MemoryWriteEvent>.make()
  run writes.append(MemoryWriteEvent {
    readyAt: SystemClock.make(0, 0),
    action: MemoryWriteAction.Accept {count: 64},
  })
  let mut memory = run MemoryByteDuplex.make(move reads, move writes, 64, 8, Option<i32>.none())

  let mut socket = run WebSocket.make(Transport.plain(&mut memory), Role.Server, Options.defaults(), b"")
  match run socket.readEvent(Option<Instant>.none()) {
    Event.Text {..} => {
      if socket.messageText() != "ping" { return 1 }
    }
    _ => { return 2 }
  }
  run socket.writeText("pong", Option<Instant>.none())
  drop socket
  // An unmasked Text frame: 0x81, length 4, then "pong".
  if memory.outbound() != b"\x81\x04pong" { return 3 }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed<E>(error: E) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 1
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut clock = OsMonotonicClock.make()
  let mut random = OsRandom.make()
  return run Effect.catchAll(program(), failed)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
    |> Effect.provideMut<MonotonicClock>(&mut clock)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Random>(&mut random)
}
```

Import as `WebSocket` with `import silk.http.websocket_stream { WebSocket }`.

<a id="WebSocket"></a>

## `WebSocket`

```silk
pub struct WebSocket<P>
```

A WebSocket session that owns its transport `P`.

### Details
Make it with [`WebSocket.make`](#WebSocket.impl.make) after the opening handshake. `P` must provide `HttpTransport`,
as `NativeTransport` of `silk.http.exchange_native` does for a socket or a TLS connection.

<a id="WebSocket.impl"></a>

## Implementation `WebSocket<P>`

```silk

```

<a id="WebSocket.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make(
    transport: P,
    side: Role,
    options: Options,
    buffered: &[u8],
  ) -> WebSocket<P> ! StreamError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator | &mut Random
```

Returns an open session for `role` over `transport`.

#### Details
`buffered` holds bytes that were read with the handshake and come before any later read. A
client draws the seed of its mask keys from `Random`.

#### Errors
`Protocol` with `InvalidLimits` if `maxMessageBytes` or `readCapacity` is zero.
`OutOfMemoryError` if the buffers cannot be allocated.

```silk
    &mut P provides &HttpTransport from &mut HttpTransport | &mut MonotonicClock | &mut Allocator | &mut Random
```

Sends a Close, and flushes it. Then read with `readEvent` until the `Close` event of the peer.

#### Details
`data` gives the code and reason. With `None`, the Close has no payload. It does nothing if
this side already sent Close.

#### Errors
`Protocol` if the session failed, `Io` if the transport fails or `deadline` passes.

<a id="ReadHalf"></a>

## `ReadHalf`

```silk
pub struct ReadHalf<R, W>
```

The receiving half of a split session. One fiber reads with it.

### Details
[`ReadHalf.readEvent`](#ReadHalf.impl.readEvent) answers a Ping with a Pong and a Close with a Close. It sends the answer
at once when no [`WriteHalf`](#WriteHalf) is sending, or else the writer that sends sends it next.

<a id="WriteHalf"></a>

## `WriteHalf`

```silk
pub struct WriteHalf<W>
```

A sending handle of a split session. Clone it with [`WriteHalf.clone`](#WriteHalf.impl.clone) for each fiber that sends.

### Details
Each send waits until no other writer is sending, so frames are never mixed. A Close from the
peer, or a failure of the reader, makes later sends fail.

<a id="fromHalves"></a>

## `fromHalves`

```silk
pub effect fn fromHalves<R, W>(halves: TransportHalves<R, W>, parts: Parts) -> Split<R, W>
! OutOfMemoryError
? &mut Allocator
```

Makes a split session from the halves of a transport and the [`Parts`](#Parts) of a session.

### When to use
Call it with the halves of the transport that [`WebSocket.detach`](#WebSocket.impl.detach) gave you, for example from
`Connection.split` of `silk.net.socket_native`.

### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the shared state cannot be allocated.

<a id="ReadHalf.impl.readEvent"></a>

### Method `readEvent`

```silk
pub effect fn readEvent(self: &mut Self, deadline: Option<Instant>) -> Event
  ! StreamError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator | &mut MonotonicClock | &mut Random
  where
    &mut R provides &HttpTransport from &mut HttpTransport | &mut MonotonicClock | &mut Allocator | &mut Random,
    &mut W provides &HttpTransport from &mut HttpTransport | &mut MonotonicClock | &mut Allocator | &mut Random
```

Reads frames until one event is complete, and returns it.

#### Details
A Ping is answered and a Close is answered: at once if no writer is sending, else right after
the frame that is being sent. The message of a `Text` or `Binary` event is in
[`ReadHalf.message`](#ReadHalf.impl.message). `deadline` applies to the reads and to the answers this call sends.

#### Errors
- `Protocol` for a frame that breaks a rule, or when the session is `Closed`.
- `Io` if the transport fails or `deadline` passes, `Truncated` if it ends before a Close.
